title: AI Is Dangerous, but Not for the Reasons You Think | Sasha Luccioni | TED

blocks.en_text: So I've been an AI researcher for over a decade.
blocks.zh_text: 我做AI研究员已经十多年了。

blocks.en_text: And a couple of months ago, I got the weirdest email of my career.
blocks.zh_text: 几个月前，我收到了职业生涯中最诡异的一封邮件。

blocks.en_text: A random stranger wrote to me
blocks.zh_text: 一个陌生人写信给我，

blocks.en_text: saying that my work in AI is going to end humanity.
blocks.zh_text: 说我在AI方面的工作会终结人类。

blocks.en_text: Now I get it, AI, it's so hot right now.
blocks.zh_text: 我明白，AI现在确实太火了。

blocks.en_text: It's in the headlines pretty much every day,
blocks.zh_text: 几乎每天都能上头条，

blocks.en_text: sometimes because of really cool things
blocks.zh_text: 有时候是因为特别酷的事，

blocks.en_text: like discovering new molecules for medicine
blocks.zh_text: 比如发现用于医学的新分子，

blocks.en_text: or that dope Pope in the white puffer coat.
blocks.zh_text: 或者那位穿着白色羽绒服的酷教皇。

blocks.en_text: But other times the headlines have been really dark,
blocks.zh_text: 但有时候头条也特别黑暗，

blocks.en_text: like that chatbot telling that guy that he should divorce his wife
blocks.zh_text: 比如那个聊天机器人告诉那家伙他应该和妻子离婚，

blocks.en_text: or that AI meal planner app proposing a crowd pleasing recipe
blocks.zh_text: 或者那个AI膳食规划应用提出一个迎合大众的食谱，

blocks.en_text: featuring chlorine gas.
blocks.zh_text: 里面居然有氯气。

blocks.en_text: And in the background,
blocks.zh_text: 而在幕后，

blocks.en_text: we've heard a lot of talk about doomsday scenarios,
blocks.zh_text: 我们听到很多关于末日场景的讨论，

blocks.en_text: existential risk and the singularity,
blocks.zh_text: 存在性风险和奇点，

blocks.en_text: with letters being written and events being organized
blocks.zh_text: 人们写公开信、组织活动，

blocks.en_text: to make sure that doesn't happen.
blocks.zh_text: 来确保这些不会发生。

blocks.en_text: Now I'm a researcher who studies AI's impacts on society,
blocks.zh_text: 我是个研究AI对社会影响的研究员，

blocks.en_text: and I don't know what's going to happen in 10 or 20 years,
blocks.zh_text: 我不知道10年或20年后会发生什么，

blocks.en_text: and nobody really does.
blocks.zh_text: 也没人真的知道。

blocks.en_text: But what I do know is that there's some pretty nasty things going on right now,
blocks.zh_text: 但我知道的是，现在就有一些相当糟糕的事情正在发生，

blocks.en_text: because AI doesn't exist in a vacuum.
blocks.zh_text: 因为AI不是存在于真空中的。

blocks.en_text: It is part of society, and it has impacts on people and the planet.
blocks.zh_text: 它是社会的一部分，它对人和地球都有影响。

blocks.en_text: AI models can contribute to climate change.
blocks.zh_text: AI模型会加剧气候变化。

blocks.en_text: Their training data uses art and books created by artists
blocks.zh_text: 它们的训练数据使用了艺术家创作的艺术作品和书籍

blocks.en_text: and authors without their consent.
blocks.zh_text: 以及作者的作品，却没有征得他们的同意。

blocks.en_text: And its deployment can discriminate against entire communities.
blocks.zh_text: 而且它的部署会歧视整个群体。

blocks.en_text: But we need to start tracking its impacts.
blocks.zh_text: 但我们需要开始追踪它的影响。

blocks.en_text: We need to start being transparent and disclosing them and creating tools
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要开始保持透明、公开这些影响，并创造工具，

blocks.en_text: so that people understand AI better,
blocks.zh_text: 让人们更好地理解AI，

blocks.en_text: so that hopefully future generations of AI models
blocks.zh_text: 这样希望未来几代AI模型

blocks.en_text: are going to be more trustworthy, sustainable,
blocks.zh_text: 会变得更值得信赖、更可持续，

blocks.en_text: maybe less likely to kill us, if that's what you're into.
blocks.zh_text: 也许更不容易杀死我们，如果你在意这个的话。

blocks.en_text: But let's start with sustainability,
blocks.zh_text: 但让我们从可持续性说起，

blocks.en_text: because that cloud that AI models live on is actually made out of metal, plastic,
blocks.zh_text: 因为AI模型所栖身的那片云其实是由金属、塑料制成的，

blocks.en_text: and powered by vast amounts of energy.
blocks.zh_text: 并且由大量能源驱动。

blocks.en_text: And each time you query an AI model, it comes with a cost to the planet.
blocks.zh_text: 每次你查询一个AI模型，都会给地球带来代价。

blocks.en_text: Last year, I was part of the BigScience initiative,
blocks.zh_text: 去年，我参与了BigScience计划，

blocks.en_text: which brought together a thousand researchers
blocks.zh_text: 它汇集了一千名研究员

blocks.en_text: from all over the world to create Bloom,
blocks.zh_text: 来自世界各地，共同创建了Bloom，

blocks.en_text: the first open large language model, like ChatGPT,
blocks.zh_text: 这是第一个开放的大语言模型，类似ChatGPT，

blocks.en_text: but with an emphasis on ethics, transparency and consent.
blocks.zh_text: 但强调伦理、透明度和知情同意。

blocks.en_text: And the study I led that looked at Bloom's environmental impacts
blocks.zh_text: 而我主导的那项研究考察了 Bloom 对环境的影响

blocks.en_text: found that just training it used as much energy
blocks.zh_text: 发现光是训练它就消耗了相当于

blocks.en_text: as 30 homes in a whole year
blocks.zh_text: 30 户家庭一整年的用电量

blocks.en_text: and emitted 25 tons of carbon dioxide,
blocks.zh_text: 并排放了 25 吨二氧化碳，

blocks.en_text: which is like driving your car five times around the planet
blocks.zh_text: 相当于开着你的车绕地球五圈

blocks.en_text: just so somebody can use this model to tell a knock-knock joke.
blocks.zh_text: 就为了让某个人用这个模型讲个敲门笑话。

blocks.en_text: And this might not seem like a lot,
blocks.zh_text: 这看起来可能不算多，

blocks.en_text: but other similar large language models,
blocks.zh_text: 但其他类似的大型语言模型，

blocks.en_text: like GPT-3,
blocks.zh_text: 比如 GPT-3，

blocks.en_text: emit 20 times more carbon.
blocks.zh_text: 排放的碳是它的 20 倍。

blocks.en_text: But the thing is, tech companies aren't measuring this stuff.
blocks.zh_text: 但问题是，科技公司并没有在测量这些东西。

blocks.en_text: They're not disclosing it.
blocks.zh_text: 他们也没有公开。

blocks.en_text: And so this is probably only the tip of the iceberg,
blocks.zh_text: 所以这很可能只是冰山一角，

blocks.en_text: even if it is a melting one.
blocks.zh_text: 哪怕这座冰山本身正在融化。

blocks.en_text: And in recent years we've seen AI models balloon in size
blocks.zh_text: 近年来我们看到 AI 模型的规模急剧膨胀

blocks.en_text: because the current trend in AI is "bigger is better."
blocks.zh_text: 因为当下 AI 界的潮流是“越大越好”。

blocks.en_text: But please don't get me started on why that's the case.
blocks.zh_text: 但请别让我开始讲为什么会这样。

blocks.en_text: In any case, we've seen large language models in particular
blocks.zh_text: 无论如何，我们看到尤其是大型语言模型

blocks.en_text: grow 2,000 times in size over the last five years.
blocks.zh_text: 在过去五年里规模增长了两千倍。

blocks.en_text: And of course, their environmental costs are rising as well.
blocks.zh_text: 当然，它们的环境成本也在上升。

blocks.en_text: The most recent work I led, found that switching out a smaller,
blocks.zh_text: 我最近主导的研究发现，把一个更小、

blocks.en_text: more efficient model for a larger language model
blocks.zh_text: 更高效的模型换成一个更大的语言模型

blocks.en_text: emits 14 times more carbon for the same task.
blocks.zh_text: 完成同样的任务会多排放 14 倍的碳。

blocks.en_text: Like telling that knock-knock joke.
blocks.zh_text: 比如讲那个敲门笑话。

blocks.en_text: And as we're putting in these models into cell phones and search engines
blocks.zh_text: 而随着我们把这些模型装进手机、搜索引擎

blocks.en_text: and smart fridges and speakers,
blocks.zh_text: 智能冰箱和音箱里，

blocks.en_text: the environmental costs are really piling up quickly.
blocks.zh_text: 环境成本真的在迅速累积。

blocks.en_text: So instead of focusing on some future existential risks,
blocks.zh_text: 所以与其关注某些未来的生存风险，

blocks.en_text: let's talk about current tangible impacts
blocks.zh_text: 不如谈谈当下实实在在的影响

blocks.en_text: and tools we can create to measure and mitigate these impacts.
blocks.zh_text: 以及我们能开发出来衡量和减轻这些影响的工具。

blocks.en_text: I helped create CodeCarbon,
blocks.zh_text: 我参与开发了 CodeCarbon，

blocks.en_text: a tool that runs in parallel to AI training code
blocks.zh_text: 这个工具与 AI 训练代码并行运行

blocks.en_text: that estimates the amount of energy it consumes
blocks.zh_text: 估算它消耗的能量

blocks.en_text: and the amount of carbon it emits.
blocks.zh_text: 以及它排放的碳量。

blocks.en_text: And using a tool like this can help us make informed choices,
blocks.zh_text: 使用这样的工具能帮我们做出明智的选择，

blocks.en_text: like choosing one model over the other because it's more sustainable,
blocks.zh_text: 比如选择某个模型而不是另一个，因为它更可持续，

blocks.en_text: or deploying AI models on renewable energy,
blocks.zh_text: 或者把 AI 模型部署在使用可再生能源的地方，

blocks.en_text: which can drastically reduce their emissions.
blocks.zh_text: 这能大幅减少它们的排放。

blocks.en_text: But let's talk about other things
blocks.zh_text: 但我们来谈谈其他方面

blocks.en_text: because there's other impacts of AI apart from sustainability.
blocks.zh_text: 因为除了可持续性，AI 还有其他影响。

blocks.en_text: For example, it's been really hard for artists and authors
blocks.zh_text: 例如，艺术家和作者一直很难

blocks.en_text: to prove that their life's work has been used for training AI models
blocks.zh_text: 证明他们毕生的作品被用来训练 AI 模型

blocks.en_text: without their consent.
blocks.zh_text: 而且未经他们同意。

blocks.en_text: And if you want to sue someone, you tend to need proof, right?
blocks.zh_text: 而如果你想起诉某人，你往往需要证据，对吧？

blocks.en_text: So Spawning.ai, an organization that was founded by artists,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，Spawning.ai，一个由艺术家创立的组织，

blocks.en_text: created this really cool tool called “Have I Been Trained?”
blocks.zh_text: 开发了一个非常酷的工具，叫“Have I Been Trained?”（我被训练过吗？）

blocks.en_text: And it lets you search these massive data sets
blocks.zh_text: 它可以让你搜索这些庞大的数据集

blocks.en_text: to see what they have on you.
blocks.zh_text: 看看里面有什么关于你的内容。

blocks.en_text: Now, I admit it, I was curious.
blocks.zh_text: 我承认，我很好奇。

blocks.en_text: I searched LAION-5B,
blocks.zh_text: 我搜索了LAION-5B，

blocks.en_text: which is this huge data set of images and text,
blocks.zh_text: 这是一个包含图像和文本的巨型数据集，

blocks.en_text: to see if any images of me were in there.
blocks.zh_text: 看看里面有没有我的照片。

blocks.en_text: Now those two first images,
blocks.zh_text: 那前两张图片，

blocks.en_text: that's me from events I've spoken at.
blocks.zh_text: 是我在演讲活动上的照片。

blocks.en_text: But the rest of the images, none of those are me.
blocks.zh_text: 但其余的图片，没有一张是我。

blocks.en_text: They're probably of other women named Sasha
blocks.zh_text: 它们很可能是其他叫Sasha的女性

blocks.en_text: who put photographs of themselves up on the internet.
blocks.zh_text: 把自己照片传到网上的。

blocks.en_text: And this can probably explain why,
blocks.zh_text: 这大概能解释为什么，

blocks.en_text: when I query an image generation model
blocks.zh_text: 当我让一个图像生成模型

blocks.en_text: to generate a photograph of a woman named Sasha,
blocks.zh_text: 生成一张叫Sasha的女性的照片时，

blocks.en_text: more often than not I get images of bikini models.
blocks.zh_text: 我得到的往往是比基尼模特的图片。

blocks.en_text: Sometimes they have two arms,
blocks.zh_text: 有时候她们有两条胳膊，

blocks.en_text: sometimes they have three arms,
blocks.zh_text: 有时候有三条胳膊，

blocks.en_text: but they rarely have any clothes on.
blocks.zh_text: 但她们很少穿着衣服。

blocks.en_text: And while it can be interesting for people like you and me
blocks.zh_text: 虽然搜索这些数据集

blocks.en_text: to search these data sets,
blocks.zh_text: 对你我这样的人来说可能挺有意思，

blocks.en_text: for artists like Karla Ortiz,
blocks.zh_text: 但对像Karla Ortiz这样的艺术家来说，

blocks.en_text: this provides crucial evidence that her life's work, her artwork,
blocks.zh_text: 这提供了关键证据，证明她毕生的作品、她的艺术创作，

blocks.en_text: was used for training AI models without her consent,
blocks.zh_text: 在未经她同意的情况下被用于训练AI模型，

blocks.en_text: and she and two artists used this as evidence
blocks.zh_text: 她和另外两位艺术家以此作为证据

blocks.en_text: to file a class action lawsuit against AI companies
blocks.zh_text: 对AI公司提起集体诉讼

blocks.en_text: for copyright infringement.
blocks.zh_text: 指控其侵犯版权。

blocks.en_text: And most recently --
blocks.zh_text: 而最近——

blocks.en_text: And most recently Spawning.ai partnered up with Hugging Face,
blocks.zh_text: 而最近Spawning.ai与Hugging Face合作，

blocks.en_text: the company where I work at,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是我工作的公司，

blocks.en_text: to create opt-in and opt-out mechanisms for creating these data sets.
blocks.zh_text: 为创建这些数据集建立了选择加入和选择退出的机制。

blocks.en_text: Because artwork created by humans shouldn’t be an all-you-can-eat buffet
blocks.zh_text: 因为人类创作的艺术作品不该成为任人随意取用的自助餐

blocks.en_text: for training AI language models.
blocks.zh_text: 用来训练AI语言模型。

blocks.en_text: The very last thing I want to talk about is bias.
blocks.zh_text: 我最后想谈的是偏见。

blocks.en_text: You probably hear about this a lot.
blocks.zh_text: 你可能经常听到这个话题。

blocks.en_text: Formally speaking, it's when AI models encode patterns and beliefs
blocks.zh_text: 正式来说，它是指AI模型编码了某些模式和信念，

blocks.en_text: that can represent stereotypes or racism and sexism.
blocks.zh_text: 这些模式和信念可能代表刻板印象、种族主义和性别歧视。

blocks.en_text: One of my heroes, Dr. Joy Buolamwini, experienced this firsthand
blocks.zh_text: 我心目中的英雄之一，Joy Buolamwini博士，亲身经历过这种情况，

blocks.en_text: when she realized that AI systems wouldn't even detect her face
blocks.zh_text: 她发现AI系统甚至无法识别她的脸

blocks.en_text: unless she was wearing a white-colored mask.
blocks.zh_text: 除非她戴着一个白色的面具。

blocks.en_text: Digging deeper, she found that common facial recognition systems
blocks.zh_text: 深入调查后，她发现常见的面部识别系统

blocks.en_text: were vastly worse for women of color compared to white men.
blocks.zh_text: 对有色人种女性的识别效果远差于白人男性。

blocks.en_text: And when biased models like this are deployed in law enforcement settings,
blocks.zh_text: 当这种带有偏见的模型被部署到执法场景中时，

blocks.en_text: this can result in false accusations, even wrongful imprisonment,
blocks.zh_text: 可能导致错误指控，甚至错误监禁，

blocks.en_text: which we've seen happen to multiple people in recent months.
blocks.zh_text: 近几个月我们已经看到多起这样的事件发生在不同人身上。

blocks.en_text: For example, Porcha Woodruff was wrongfully accused of carjacking
blocks.zh_text: 比如，Porcha Woodruff 被错误地指控劫车

blocks.en_text: at eight months pregnant
blocks.zh_text: 当时她已怀孕八个月

blocks.en_text: because an AI system wrongfully identified her.
blocks.zh_text: 因为一个人工智能系统错误地指认了她。

blocks.en_text: But sadly, these systems are black boxes,
blocks.zh_text: 但遗憾的是，这些系统都是黑箱，

blocks.en_text: and even their creators can't say exactly why they work the way they do.
blocks.zh_text: 就连它们的创造者也说不清它们为什么会这样运作。

blocks.en_text: And for example, for image generation systems,
blocks.zh_text: 再比如，对于图像生成系统来说，

blocks.en_text: if they're used in contexts like generating a forensic sketch
blocks.zh_text: 如果它们被用在生成嫌疑人素描这类场景中，

blocks.en_text: based on a description of a perpetrator,
blocks.zh_text: 根据对罪犯的描述来生成画像，

blocks.en_text: they take all those biases and they spit them back out
blocks.zh_text: 它们会把这些偏见全都吐出来，

blocks.en_text: for terms like dangerous criminal, terrorists or gang member,
blocks.zh_text: 比如遇到“危险罪犯”“恐怖分子”或“帮派成员”这些词时，

blocks.en_text: which of course is super dangerous
blocks.zh_text: 这当然非常危险，

blocks.en_text: when these tools are deployed in society.
blocks.zh_text: 尤其是当这些工具被部署到社会中时。

blocks.en_text: And so in order to understand these tools better,
blocks.zh_text: 所以为了更好地理解这些工具，

blocks.en_text: I created this tool called the Stable Bias Explorer,
blocks.zh_text: 我做了这个叫 Stable Bias Explorer 的工具，

blocks.en_text: which lets you explore the bias of image generation models
blocks.zh_text: 它可以让你探索图像生成模型的偏见，

blocks.en_text: through the lens of professions.
blocks.zh_text: 从职业的角度来看。

blocks.en_text: So try to picture a scientist in your mind.
blocks.zh_text: 那你在脑海里想象一位科学家。

blocks.en_text: Don't look at me.
blocks.zh_text: 别看我。

blocks.en_text: What do you see?
blocks.zh_text: 你看到了什么？

blocks.en_text: A lot of the same thing, right?
blocks.zh_text: 很多都差不多，对吧？

blocks.en_text: Men in glasses and lab coats.
blocks.zh_text: 戴眼镜、穿白大褂的男人。

blocks.en_text: And none of them look like me.
blocks.zh_text: 没有一个长得像我。

blocks.en_text: And the thing is,
blocks.zh_text: 而问题是，

blocks.en_text: is that we looked at all these different image generation models
blocks.zh_text: 我们研究了所有这些不同的图像生成模型

blocks.en_text: and found a lot of the same thing:
blocks.zh_text: 发现了大量相同的情况：

blocks.en_text: significant representation of whiteness and masculinity
blocks.zh_text: 白人和男性形象占比极高

blocks.en_text: across all 150 professions that we looked at,
blocks.zh_text: 在我们研究的所有150种职业中都是如此，

blocks.en_text: even if compared to the real world,
blocks.zh_text: 即使跟现实世界相比也是如此，

blocks.en_text: the US Labor Bureau of Statistics.
blocks.zh_text: 也就是美国劳工统计局的数据。

blocks.en_text: These models show lawyers as men,
blocks.zh_text: 这些模型把律师呈现为男性，

blocks.en_text: and CEOs as men, almost 100 percent of the time,
blocks.zh_text: 把CEO呈现为男性，几乎百分之百都是这样，

blocks.en_text: even though we all know not all of them are white and male.
blocks.zh_text: 尽管我们都知道并非所有律师和CEO都是白人和男性。

blocks.en_text: And sadly, my tool hasn't been used to write legislation yet.
blocks.zh_text: 遗憾的是，我的工具还没被用来起草法律。

blocks.en_text: But I recently presented it at a UN event about gender bias
blocks.zh_text: 但我最近在一个关于性别偏见的联合国活动上展示了它，

blocks.en_text: as an example of how we can make tools for people from all walks of life,
blocks.zh_text: 作为例子说明我们如何能为各行各业的人打造工具，

blocks.en_text: even those who don't know how to code,
blocks.zh_text: 甚至是那些不会编程的人，

blocks.en_text: to engage with and better understand AI because we use professions,
blocks.zh_text: 让他们参与进来、更好地理解AI，因为我们用的是职业，

blocks.en_text: but you can use any terms that are of interest to you.
blocks.zh_text: 但你也可以用任何你感兴趣的词。

blocks.en_text: And as these models are being deployed,
blocks.zh_text: 而随着这些模型被部署，

blocks.en_text: are being woven into the very fabric of our societies,
blocks.zh_text: 被编织进我们社会的肌理之中，

blocks.en_text: our cell phones, our social media feeds,
blocks.zh_text: 我们的手机、我们的社交媒体信息流，

blocks.en_text: even our justice systems and our economies have AI in them.
blocks.zh_text: 甚至我们的司法系统和经济体里都有人工智能。

blocks.en_text: And it's really important that AI stays accessible
blocks.zh_text: 人工智能保持可及性真的非常重要，

blocks.en_text: so that we know both how it works and when it doesn't work.
blocks.zh_text: 这样我们才能既知道它如何运作，也知道它何时不奏效。

blocks.en_text: And there's no single solution for really complex things like bias
blocks.zh_text: 而且对于像偏见这样真正复杂的问题，并没有单一的解决方案

blocks.en_text: or copyright or climate change.
blocks.zh_text: 或者版权，或者气候变化。

blocks.en_text: But by creating tools to measure AI's impact,
blocks.zh_text: 但通过创造衡量AI影响的工具，

blocks.en_text: we can start getting an idea of how bad they are
blocks.zh_text: 我们就能开始了解它们有多糟糕

blocks.en_text: and start addressing them as we go.
blocks.zh_text: 并在前进的过程中着手解决它们。

blocks.en_text: Start creating guardrails to protect society and the planet.
blocks.zh_text: 开始建立防护栏来保护社会和地球。

blocks.en_text: And once we have this information,
blocks.zh_text: 一旦我们掌握了这些信息，

blocks.en_text: companies can use it in order to say,
blocks.zh_text: 公司就可以利用它来说，

blocks.en_text: OK, we're going to choose this model because it's more sustainable,
blocks.zh_text: 好，我们要选这个模型，因为它更可持续，

blocks.en_text: this model because it respects copyright.
blocks.zh_text: 选这个模型，因为它尊重版权。

blocks.en_text: Legislators who really need information to write laws,
blocks.zh_text: 真正需要信息来制定法律的立法者，

blocks.en_text: can use these tools to develop new regulation mechanisms
blocks.zh_text: 可以利用这些工具来开发新的监管机制

blocks.en_text: or governance for AI as it gets deployed into society.
blocks.zh_text: 或者随着AI被部署到社会中，对它进行治理。

blocks.en_text: And users like you and me can use this information
blocks.zh_text: 而像你我这样的用户，可以利用这些信息

blocks.en_text: to choose AI models that we can trust,
blocks.zh_text: 来选择我们可以信任的AI模型，

blocks.en_text: not to misrepresent us and not to misuse our data.
blocks.zh_text: 不会歪曲我们、也不会滥用我们数据的模型。

blocks.en_text: But what did I reply to that email
blocks.zh_text: 但我对那封邮件是怎么回复的？

blocks.en_text: that said that my work is going to destroy humanity?
blocks.zh_text: 那封说我的工作会毁灭人类的邮件？

blocks.en_text: I said that focusing on AI's future existential risks
blocks.zh_text: 我说，把注意力放在AI未来的生存风险上

blocks.en_text: is a distraction from its current,
blocks.zh_text: 会让人忽视它当前

blocks.en_text: very tangible impacts
blocks.zh_text: 非常切实的影响

blocks.en_text: and the work we should be doing right now, or even yesterday,
blocks.zh_text: 以及我们现在、甚至昨天就该做的、

blocks.en_text: for reducing these impacts.
blocks.zh_text: 用来减少这些影响的工作。

blocks.en_text: Because yes, AI is moving quickly, but it's not a done deal.
blocks.zh_text: 因为没错，AI发展得很快，但这不是已成定局的事。

blocks.en_text: We're building the road as we walk it,
blocks.zh_text: 我们是一边走一边修路，

blocks.en_text: and we can collectively decide what direction we want to go in together.
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以共同决定要一起往哪个方向走。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。
